genZNote: Looks like Neisseria on Gram stain, fails to ferment a single carbohydrate, and still ends up causing your sinus infection.

habitat.hostAssociation: Common commensal, especially in children; opportunistic respiratory pathogen

culture.growthCharacteristics: Aerobic, grows on routine non-selective media (unlike Neisseria/Haemophilus)
culture.colonyMorphology: Opaque, grayish-white colonies that can be pushed intact across the agar surface ("hockey puck sign")

identificationClues: Gram-negative diplococci resembling Neisseria on Gram stain
Oxidase positive but does NOT ferment carbohydrates, unlike Neisseria species
"Hockey puck sign" — colony can be pushed intact across the agar
DNase positive — helps distinguish from Neisseria

diseases: Bronchitis and pneumonia exacerbations, especially in COPD patients
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the three classic bacterial causes of otitis media/sinusitis in children (with S. pneumoniae and non-typeable H. influenzae); frequent cause of COPD exacerbations in adults
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Non-fermenting biochemistry plus the hockey-puck colony sign distinguish it from pathogenic Neisseria species on routine workup

examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Resembles Neisseria on Gram stain but does not ferment carbohydrates
